value.rationale: The motivating work highlights how the number of opinion classes affects asymptotic behavior, but lacks general-k quantitative spectral instability. This theorem gives exact rate scaling and a non-obvious extreme-state localization mechanism, revealing a k-scale symmetry-breaking growth time despite k^2-scale reflecting diffusion relaxation. Both scaling constants and profile are natural and can guide near-uniform perturbation analysis, independent of any full nonlinear basin classification.
